---
title: Analysis
llms-description: "The `inspect_swarm:metrics` and `inspect_swarm:ledger` store entries and the swarm columns for Inspect's `samples_df()`; read it to analyse a swarm's usage, cost, communication and waits after a run."
---

## Overview

When the swarm ends it writes two entries to the sample store, each also logged as a `SwarmEvent` of kind `metrics` or `ledger` whose `data` is the entry:

- `inspect_swarm:metrics`: tokens, cost and time for the swarm and each member, and counts of how each member acted, checked its work, communicated and waited ([Metrics](#metrics)).
- `inspect_swarm:ledger`: the swarm's accounting. Its budget, caps, the usage of each member, model calls that errored or reported no usage, unpriced models, and what stopped the swarm ([The ledger](#the-ledger)).

The result record is an event in the transcript, which `swarm_result(sample)` reads from a sample. It is described in [Scoring](scoring.qmd#the-result-record).

## Metrics

For the swarm:

- `tokens`, `cost`: everything in the swarm: members, controller and final step.
- `wall_clock`: seconds from the swarm's start to its end.
- `never_acted`: members with no completed model call.
- `steps_to_answer`: completed model calls of the member whose output is the answer, `null` with no answer. For a persistent member's answer, its calls before that answer.
- `longest_member_steps`: the largest number of completed model calls of any member.
- `critical_steps_to_answer`: the number of completed model calls on the longest chain of calls the answer depended on, across members ([The critical path](#the-critical-path)).

Step counts include cache replays and exclude failed or cancelled attempts. A member's subagents' calls count as the member's. `steps_to_answer` and `longest_member_steps` bound each member's own sequential depth from above, not the swarm's: they do not see that one member waited for or read another's work.

For each member, in roster order:

- `tokens`, `cost`: its usage, its subagents' and background work's included.
- `running_time`: seconds from its start to its end, `null` for a member never started.
- `longest_identical_tool_run`: the longest run of identical tool calls (same function and arguments), a sign of a stuck member. `null` for a bridged member: the CLI's own tool calls are not recorded; bridged host tool calls, such as the swarm's tools, are.
- `gate_checks`, `gate_passes`, `first_pass_time`: its in-loop checks ([Scoring](scoring.qmd#checks-during-the-run)).
- `comm`, `waits`, `waits_by_outcome`, `wait_time`, `idle_time`: below.
- `holds`, `held_time`: the turn boundaries at which a controller's callbacks held it, and the seconds it was held. `running_time` includes them ([Boundary callbacks](#boundary-callbacks)). A persistent member's idle holds count too.
- `activations`, `answers`, `awaiting_work_time`: for a [persistent member](members.qmd#persistent-members), the activations it began (1 at its start, one more for each wake), the answers it gave, and the part of `held_time` it spent idle, waiting for a wake or its end. All 0 for other members.

### The critical path

`critical_steps_to_answer` is the measure to read latency by: how many model calls the answer took one after another, given that members work in parallel but wait on and build on each other. A member that waits for a peer's file and then answers in three steps has `steps_to_answer` 3, but if the peer took ten steps to write that file, the answer took at least 11.

Each member's calls, its subagents' and background work's included, form one chain in the order they began. Chains link between members in two ways:

- A channel's result follows the records it showed, as the channel reports them. It links to each record's sender at the point the record was committed, so the sender's work after a send or write is not linked. `shared_memory`: a view of a file follows every write in its history, a view of a deleted file follows the delete, and a `swarm_wait` result follows the write of each file it reports. Directory listings and the `changes` status line make no link. `messages`: `read_messages` follows the messages it returned, and a `swarm_wait` result that reports messages follows every unread message it counts. A message sent with `wake=False` links when it is read, or when a wait that reports messages counts it. A custom channel links what it reports ([Channels](channels.qmd#writing-a-channel)).
- A `swarm_wait` result that names a member's end follows all of that member's calls.

The chain ends when the answering member ends, after its background work has finished, since that work can still change the member's output. For a persistent member's answer, it ends at that answer.

The number over-counts work inside a member. Parallel and background subagents, tool calls of one turn, and any other concurrent work count one after another, and the answering member's background work after its agent returned, its reads included, counts whether or not it changed the answer. That excess reaches peers through the member's later writes.

The number also misses links. Only channel results and `swarm_wait` make them, so information that members share in other ways adds none: a shared sandbox, a shared volume, a service, a custom channel that reports no dependencies, a shared tool or store key, or a controller that passes one member's result to another. Counts alone make no link either: the unread-message count and the line of changed files on other results, and `list_members`. Missed links can only lower the number.

With both effects it is not a bound on true causal depth in either direction. A nested swarm's channels make no link for the outer swarm; its own metrics count it.

It is `null` when there is no answer, when the answering member has no recorded end, when the evidence names a record no recorded commit made (with a warning in the log), and for a sample resumed from a checkpoint. Metrics written by earlier versions do not have it.

### Communication

Each member's `comm` has an entry, by channel name, for each channel with records, such as `shared_memory`:

- `records` and `record_bytes`: its writes or messages delivered to the channel, and their size.
- `rejections`: its writes or messages the swarm refused, by the control that refused them, such as `rate`.
- `reads` and `listings`: its views of files and of directories, and its `read_messages` results that showed messages.

A member's subagents count as the member. Every member has an entry for every such channel the swarm opened, zeros included. A swarm with none (`filesystem` only, or `channels=[]`) has `comm` `{}` for every member: communication through files is observed, not recorded, so it is not reported as zero ([Channels](channels.qmd#shared-files-are-observed-not-recorded)).

### Waits

Each member's metrics count its `swarm_wait` calls, its subagents' included:

- `waits`: the number of waits.
- `waits_by_outcome`: that number by what ended each wait: `news` (a changed file or an ended member), `all_waiting`, `stopping`, `member_ending`, `timeout` or `cancelled`. An outcome that ended no wait is left out.
- `wait_time`: the waits' total seconds. Waits of a member's subagents that overlap each count.
- `idle_time`: the seconds the member did nothing but wait: its own agent in `swarm_wait`, not yet released, and none of its background work running. A subagent's wait adds to `wait_time` but not to `idle_time`.

In a swarm with no `swarm_wait` (`filesystem` only, or `channels=[]`) the four are `null`, so 0 means the wait was offered and unused. Waiting is wall-clock time, so a member's `running_time` includes it.

### Boundary callbacks

When a controller holds a member at turn boundaries ([Controllers](controllers.qmd#boundary-callbacks)), the swarm writes two kinds of `SwarmEvent` in the member's span, with `member` set. Neither holds message text.

`boundary`, once for each boundary where callbacks ran, and for each hold of a persistent member after an answer, callbacks or not:

- `boundary`: the boundary's index. `after`: what the conversation ended with.
- `origins`: the origins of the callbacks that ran, in order. `held_for`: the seconds the member was held.
- `messages`: the number of messages `before` and `after`.
- `outcome`: `continue` (any change is in the conversation), `end` (with `origin`), `stop`, `error` (a callback raised, or its result was invalid; with `origin` and `error`, the error's type), `rejected` (applying the change failed, such as at the member's message limit; with `error`) or `cancelled` (a cancellation from outside the swarm).

`changed`, once for each callback whose result differed from what it received, with its `boundary` and `origin`:

- `added`: each new message's `id`, `hash` and `index` in the result.
- `removed`: the ids of messages no longer there.
- `replaced`: each message kept under its id with new content, with its `id` and its hashes `before` and `after`.
- `order`: the result's ids in order, only when the kept messages changed their order.
- `applied`: whether the change is in the member's conversation. It is `false` when a later callback ended the member or raised, the swarm stopped, or the change was rejected.

A hash is the SHA-256 of the message as the log serializes it, without its id (a value JSON cannot hold counts as null, and text UTF-8 cannot encode is escaped), so a change can be matched to the messages in a later `ModelEvent`'s input. When a callback rewrites the conversation, compaction summaries that describe messages it changed are removed, and the removal is one more `changed` event with origin `swarm`. A persistent member's wake input is a `changed` event with origin `swarm` too, before the callbacks' own.

### Persistent members

A [persistent member](members.qmd#persistent-members) writes one `answer` event for each answer, in its span, with `answer`, the answer's index from 0. In the result record, its `MemberResult` has `persistent` true and `answer_times`, the swarm time of each answer. `FinalRecord.answer`, and the `final` event's `answer`, say which of the chosen member's answers is the swarm's; they are `null` for other members.

### Operator actions

When an operator sends a member a message with `inspect ctl sample agent message` ([Operators](operators.qmd)), the swarm writes one `operator_message` event in the member's span, with `member` set. It holds no text:

- `id`: the swarm's id for the message, `op-1`, `op-2` and so on in the order the swarm accepted them. The message's `metadata` has the same id under `inspect_swarm`.
- `message_id`: the id of the `ChatMessageUser` the swarm posted. Messages the member's loop takes together are merged into one user message with a new id, so look for the text in the member's messages rather than for this id.
- `interrupt`: whether the operator asked to interrupt the member's turn. `in_turn`: whether the member was in a turn when the message was posted.
- `outcome`: `drained` when the member's loop took the message off its channel, or `not_drained` when the member ended first.
- `boundary`: for a drained message, the index of the turn boundary the loop goes on from: the boundary where it took the message, or after an interrupt the next one. `recovery`: whether the loop took it while recovering from an interrupt. Both are `null` for `not_drained`.

`drained` does not mean that a model saw the message. The member's conversation can refuse it at its message limit, a boundary callback can remove it, and the member can end before its next model call. The member's messages and the `ModelEvent` inputs show where it arrived.

A member's `member_result` event, its `MemberResult` in the result record and its ledger line have `end_origin`: who asked the member to end, when an end request decided how it ended. It is `operator` for `inspect ctl sample agent stop`, the origin a controller gave `MemberHandle.end()`, or `null` when no end request did, as for a submission, a member limit or the swarm's own stop.

### Wiring checks

The metrics also check that members are wired to the channels. `tools_unwired` lists, in a swarm with a channel that has tools, the native members with a completed model call whose loops never resolved `swarm_tools()`. Bridged members are exempt, so this metric does not detect a CLI built without `swarm_bridged_tools()`. A member listed there did not get what the channel offers, so it ran a different experiment from the one configured.

## Samples dataframe

`inspect_swarm.analysis.SwarmColumns` adds each sample's realized cost and ledger data to Inspect's `samples_df()`. `samples_df()` needs pandas and pyarrow, which Inspect Swarm does not install:

```bash
pip install "pandas>=2.1.0" "pyarrow>=10.0.1"
```

This example uses a task with a scorer named `match`. Replace `score_match` with your task's score column (`score_<scorer name>`):

```python
from inspect_ai.analysis import SampleSummary, samples_df
from inspect_ai.scorer import value_to_float

from inspect_swarm.analysis import SwarmColumns

df = samples_df("logs", columns=SampleSummary + SwarmColumns)
df = df[~df["swarm_resumed"]]
df["score"] = df["score_match"].map(value_to_float(), na_action="ignore")
df.groupby("log")[["score", "swarm_cost"]].mean()
```

The columns:

- `swarm_cost`: the sample's priced cost in dollars, from its `model_usage`, including scorer calls. Tokens are in `SampleSummary`'s `total_tokens`.
- `swarm_complete`: no call is known to be missing from `swarm_cost`. The ledger marks the swarm's interval complete, and every model in the sample's `model_usage` is priced. Calls outside the swarm, including scorer calls, are not checked. `False` for a sample with no ledger.
- `swarm_members`: members in the roster.
- `swarm_resumed`: the sample resumed from a checkpoint, so the swarm restarted its caps from zero. Swarms now refuse checkpointing ([Restrictions](restrictions.qmd)), so only logs from earlier versions can have it true. `False` for a sample with no ledger.
- `swarm_cost_cap`, `swarm_token_cap`, `swarm_time_cap`: the swarm's caps. The time cap is in seconds.
- `swarm_errored`, `swarm_no_usage`, `swarm_unpriced`: model calls in the swarm that errored or were cancelled (retries included), that completed with no usage, and whose usage has no cost. Each makes the cost a lower bound.
- `swarm_unpriced_models`: models with tokens and no cost, from the ledger and the sample's `model_usage`, as a JSON list.

The columns read from the ledger are null for a sample with no ledger. A sample that runs two swarms keeps only the last one's ledger, while its `model_usage` covers both. The columns read the sample's `store` and `model_usage`, so do not exclude either with `samples_df(exclude_fields=...)`.

The columns hold no per-member data. `swarm_ledger()` reads a sample's whole ledger as a `SwarmLedger`, whose `members` are `MemberLedger`s with a `Meter` and `Calls` each. All are in `inspect_swarm.analysis`, and `SwarmLedger.model_json_schema()` describes every field. For example, each member's cost:

```python
from inspect_ai.log import read_eval_log

from inspect_swarm.analysis import swarm_ledger

log = read_eval_log("logs/my-eval.eval")
for sample in log.samples or []:
    ledger = swarm_ledger(sample)
    if ledger is not None:
        for m in ledger.members:
            print(sample.id, sample.epoch, m.name, m.meter.cost)
```

The metrics have no reader of their own; read them from `sample.store["inspect_swarm:metrics"]`.

## The ledger

The ledger of a two-member swarm with a cost cap of $1 and a time cap of 600 seconds:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "budget": {"cost": 1.0, "tokens": null, "time": 600.0, "reserve": 0.05, "split": "pool", "grace": 120.0, "derive": true},
  "caps": {"cost": 1.0, "tokens": null, "time": 600.0},
  "sample_limits": {"token": null, "cost": null, "message": null, "turn": null, "working": null, "time": null},
  "members": [
    {
      "name": "react-1",
      "status": "submitted",
      "bridged": false,
      "meter": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 1200, "output_tokens": 300, "total_tokens": 1500, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.0081}, "cost": 0.0081, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
      "calls": {"calls": 1, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
      "cancelled": false,
      "background_started": 0,
      "background_cancelled": 0
    },
    {
      "name": "react-2",
      "status": "submitted",
      "bridged": false,
      "meter": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 1150, "output_tokens": 280, "total_tokens": 1430, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.00765}, "cost": 0.00765, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
      "calls": {"calls": 1, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
      "cancelled": false,
      "background_started": 0,
      "background_cancelled": 0
    }
  ],
  "runtime": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": null}, "cost": 0.0, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "final": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": null}, "cost": 0.0, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "swarm": {"usage": {"input_tokens": 2350, "output_tokens": 580, "total_tokens": 2930, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.01575}, "cost": 0.01575, "suspended_cost": 0.0},
  "calls": {"calls": 2, "cache_replays": 0, "errored": 0, "no_usage": 0, "unpriced": 0},
  "unpriced_calls_recorded": 0,
  "sample_delta": {"input_tokens": 2350, "output_tokens": 580, "total_tokens": 2930, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.01575},
  "unattributed": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "input_tokens_cache_write": null, "input_tokens_cache_read": null, "reasoning_tokens": null, "total_cost": 0.0},
  "unpriced_models": [],
  "native_compaction_classes": [],
  "overshoot": {},
  "stop_reason": "submitted",
  "ended_by": null,
  "interrupted": false,
  "final_cancelled": false,
  "resumed": false,
  "total_complete": true,
  "attribution_complete": true
}
```

- `budget` is the `Budget` as given. `caps` are the caps the swarm applied, derived from the sample's limits or given: `cost` in dollars, `tokens`, and `time` in seconds, `null` for no cap. `sample_limits` are the sample's limits when the swarm started.
- `members` has one entry per member, in roster order. `status` is as in [How a member ends](members.qmd#how-a-member-ends), `null` for a member never started. `cancelled` means the swarm or the sample cancelled the member, so calls it had in flight are unknown. A hard stop during a background drain also sets `cancelled`; the agent's returned status is kept. So does a stop or `end()` that cancels a boundary callback while one of its model calls is in flight. `background_started` counts the tasks the member started with `background()`, and `background_cancelled` those cancelled before they finished, whose calls in flight are unknown too. `end_origin` is who asked the member to end ([Operator actions](#operator-actions)), and is left out of ledgers written before it existed.
- `meter` is the usage and cost of what a member did. `suspended_cost` is the part spent while token counting was suspended, such as approval calls.
- `calls` counts model calls: `calls` completed ones other than cache replays, `cache_replays` replayed from cache at no charge, `errored` attempts that errored or were cancelled (retries included), `no_usage` completed with no usage, and `unpriced` completed with usage but no cost.
- `runtime` meters the controller's calls and in-run verification, `final` the final step's calls, including verification, and `swarm` everything in the swarm: members, runtime and final step. The top-level `calls` counts every call in the swarm. `unpriced_calls_recorded` counts the unpriced calls the swarm's meter recorded.
- `sample_delta` is the sample's usage while the swarm ran. `unattributed` is `sample_delta` minus `swarm`: usage no meter holds, such as the tokens of approval calls.
- `unpriced_models` are models with tokens but no cost. `native_compaction_classes` are loaded model classes that can compact a conversation natively, which logs nothing, so their usage may be missing.
- `overshoot` is how far usage went past each cap, for caps it passed. Calls in flight at a stop can carry usage past a cap.
- `stop_reason` is why the swarm stopped itself: a controller's `submitted` or `all_done` (as `leaderless` returns), `verified` or `quiescence`, `controller:<reason>` for any other reason a controller returns, `swarm_cap`, `swarm_time`, or `operator` when an operator stopped the swarm with `inspect ctl sample agent stop --group`. `ended_by` is what ended it from outside: `sample_limit:<type>`, `operator` for an interrupt, or `unknown`. Each is `null` when it did not happen. Both are set when a sample limit ends the swarm during its own stop, except for `operator`: a swarm that fails or is cancelled never has `stop_reason` `operator`.
- `interrupted` means an error (a member's, the controller's or the final step's) or a cancellation ended the swarm before it finished, `final_cancelled` that the final step was cancelled, and `resumed` that the sample resumed from a checkpoint.
- `total_complete` means no call is known to be missing from the totals: nothing was cancelled or interrupted, every call reported priced usage, and no model class can compact natively. Otherwise the totals are lower bounds. `attribution_complete` adds that `unattributed` is zero.
